scope: Two separately approved sibling A2A delegations executed by the Cloudflare Worker/D1 Workflow fixture under one owner-scoped parent job and shared budget.
verified: Each endpoint returned a separate Agent Card and was bound to its own delegation target and signed usage receipt.
The first result was captured encrypted in D1, read back in the test, and composed using buildA2AResultHandoffPrompt as explicitly untrusted input for the separately approved second delegation.
The parent pool reflected the first settled usage plus the second held reservation and stayed within its shared cap.
Both child workflows reached remote_completed and settled their own signed receipt exactly once.
Restarting each completed durable Workflow returned not_dispatchable; total remote_send_claimed events remained exactly two, one per child.
notProven: Both Agent endpoints and signed receipts are controlled local fixtures, not independent commercial Provider services or production interoperability.
The second child delegation is separately approved; the test does not implement a parent controller that autonomously requests or bypasses that new approval.
This does not prove production D1 deployment, invoice issuance, funded Wallet settlement, carrier activation, or OS installation on a device.
